forecasts.reason: 238→225 steps gives about −5.3% time. True loss is about 0.12 pp, landing near the 0.7545 bar, so the seed re-roll decides it.
Pixel-weighted compute falls 4.2%. Staying in the 3×3 regime should keep the loss to 0.1–0.2 pp, much less than E018's, but separating 'regime' from 'pixels' needs more than one point.
The final EMA copy already captures most of the averaging gain, and a stronger mid-run pull slows the fast weights, so the net effect should be about zero within noise.
Label smoothing has been insensitive (E013), and the +0.2 pp bar is set against E016's inflated 0.7607.
Same commit, so the score matches the tip. The width-efficiency loss in E021 and memory-bound BN/GELU imply well under 90 TFLOP/s for the whole step.
Main-net steps are matched, so the proxy's forward over 4000 images, its training and the topk are pure overhead. Time cannot fall 5% unless epochs are later cut.

cruxes: What is the tip's true 10-seed mean, 0.7545 or nearer 0.756? This decides whether any −5% lever such as I036 or I037 is feasible.
Does proxy selection give at least +0.4 pp per main-net step? If so, it funds an epoch cut larger than its overhead, which is the only booster large enough to matter.
Which layers fall below median conv efficiency (I040)? Group 3 on 2×2/3×3 maps or group 1's memory-bound BN/GELU would make a targeted architecture cut worth roughly 1:1 in time.
structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E021.

The tip is E017: 238 steps (about 9.5 true epochs), 6.548 s. Its true mean is about 0.7545–0.755, against a 3-seed bar of 0.753.

Time:
- Steps and pixels scale time almost 1:1.
- Width cuts return about 50% of their MAC fraction as time.

Accuracy costs of the dials:
- Epochs: about 0.25 pp per 10% of time.
- Group-2 width: similar to epochs.
- Low-resolution phases: expensive, about 1 pp per 10% of time. The 3×3 final-map regime may be the reason.

Flat knobs: label smoothing, Muon lr, weight decay, LR floor. I expect the alpha exponent and per-phase label smoothing to be flat too.

The only large untested lever is proxy selection. As specified (main-net steps matched) it adds time, and it pays off only if a later epoch cut beats its overhead.

Near-line attempts are coin flips on the seeds-0–2 draw, so ideas should be judged on held-out seeds as well.
